enzyme_name: uncharacterised lactone-opening step of bacterial camphor degradation (no protein assigned)
organism_context: Pseudomonas putida ATCC 17453 / NCIMB 10007 (CAM plasmid) camphor catabolism
rationale: MetaCyc R547-RXN is the opening of the delta-lactone generated by the Baeyer-Villiger step of camphor catabolism; reviews and biochemical studies of the CAM-plasmid enzymes (the diketocamphane monooxygenases, OTEMO) assign no protein to this lactone to delta2,5-trimethylpimelyl-CoA step, and it may well be spontaneous. Catalyst unidentified, so functionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: Catabolic flux runs lactone -> ring-opened delta2,5-trimethylpimelyl-CoA on the way to beta-oxidation, i.e. the stored left-to-right sense, so ModelSEED's '<' inverts the pathway.

enzyme_name: organomercurial lyase (MerB)
organism_context: mer operons of mercury-resistant bacteria (E. coli plasmid R831, Bacillus, Cupriavidus metallidurans)
rationale: MerB is a small single-domain cytosolic lyase that performs exactly one chemical step, protonolysis of the Hg-C bond, then hands Hg(II) to the separate flavoenzyme MerA; no second catalytic activity is described in its structural or mechanistic literature.
direction_note: C-Hg protonolysis is a detoxification step and effectively irreversible; no enzyme mercurates benzene with Hg2+ and acetate, so ModelSEED's '<' is biochemically impossible.

enzyme_name: putative radical SAM pterin C-7/C-9 methylase (MJ0619)
distinct_activities: pterin C-7 methylation (radical SAM CX3CX2C motif containing Cys102)
pterin C-9 methylation (the second radical SAM CX3CX2C motif, containing Cys77)
organism_context: Methanocaldococcus jannaschii and other methanogens; demonstrated by heterologous expression in E. coli
rationale: The two methyls that distinguish methanopterin from all other pterins (C-7 and C-9) are installed by MJ0619, a single polypeptide carrying two canonical radical-SAM motifs whose separate mutagenesis uncouples C-7 from C-9 methylation; the two regiospecific methylation activities therefore sit on one chain. Assignment of this particular MetaCyc entry to MJ0619 is inferred from chemistry - the characterised enzyme acts on 7,8-dihydro-6-hydroxymethylpterin, not on the dihydromethanopterin written here.
direction_note: Methylation runs forward in methanopterin biosynthesis, but the equation's 2 SAM -> 2 SAH is the wrong cofactor couple: the methyl donor is methylenetetrahydrofolate and SAM is cleaved reductively, so the thermodynamic direction call rests on a fictitious couple.

enzyme_name: dienelactone hydrolase (chlorodienelactone hydrolase)
organism_context: modified ortho (chlorocatechol) pathway of Pseudomonas / Ralstonia / Rhodococcus opacus 1CP; here the 2,5-dichlorotoluene route
rationale: Dienelactone hydrolase is a single-domain alpha/beta-hydrolase with one Cys-His-Asp triad that performs only the dienelactone-to-maleylacetate hydrolysis; assignment to this methyl- and chloro-substituted substrate is by pathway position rather than a dedicated paper.
direction_note: Lactone hydrolysis is essentially irreversible and is the catabolic direction; the enzyme does not relactonise maleylacetate.

enzyme_name: chloromuconate cycloisomerase
organism_context: chlorocatechol pathway of Pseudomonas / Ralstonia; the Rhodococcus erythropolis (opacus) 1CP homologue is biochemically characterised
rationale: Chloromuconate cycloisomerase is a Mn2+-dependent enolase-superfamily subunit that carries out one cycloisomerisation (with chloride elimination on some substrates) in a single active site; the dehalogenating step is part of that one mechanism, not a second activity.
direction_note: The cycloisomerisation equilibrium strongly favours the muconolactone and that is also the catabolic direction, i.e. the stored left-to-right sense.

enzyme_name: 3-chlorobenzoate-3,4-dihydro-3,4-diol dehydrogenase (CbaC)
organism_context: Comamonas testosteroni (formerly Alcaligenes sp.) BR60, cba cluster on transposon Tn5271
rationale: The cis-dihydrodiol made by the multi-component 3-chlorobenzoate 3,4-dioxygenase (CbaAB) is rearomatised by the separate NAD+-dependent short-chain dehydrogenase CbaC; the dioxygenase is a multi-protein system but this step is run by a standalone single-activity dehydrogenase.
direction_note: NAD+-dependent rearomatisation of a cis-dihydrodiol is effectively irreversible forward; '<' would require NADH-driven dearomatisation of 5-chloroprotocatechuate.

enzyme_name: 3-chlorobenzoate-3,4-dihydro-3,4-diol dehydrogenase (CbaC)
organism_context: Comamonas testosteroni (Alcaligenes sp.) BR60; 3-chlorobenzoate degradation II, via protocatechuate
rationale: Same standalone NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase as rxn20897, here acting on the 3,4-diol so that rearomatisation expels chloride and yields protocatechuate; one catalytic activity on one polypeptide, the upstream dioxygenase being a separate multi-protein system.
direction_note: Rearomatisation plus chloride release makes this one-way; ModelSEED's '<' would have to chlorinate protocatechuate with NADH, which no enzyme does.

enzyme_name: none identified - presumed spontaneous HCl elimination from 3,4-dichlorobenzoate-cis-4,5-diol
organism_context: 3,4-dichlorobenzoate degradation (MetaCyc PWY-6217) in chlorobenzoate-degrading proteobacteria
rationale: Re-aromatisation of a halogenated cis-diol with loss of HCl needs no dehydrogenase and no protein has been assigned to this step; it is most plausibly chemical rather than enzymatic, so functionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: Aromatisation with chloride loss is thermodynamically one-way and cannot be driven backwards, enzyme or not.

enzyme_name: 3-chlorobenzoate hydrolytic dehalogenase (protein not identified)
organism_context: Alcaligenes sp. strain L6 - 3-chlorobenzoate to 3-hydroxybenzoate to gentisate route (MetaCyc PWY-6228)
rationale: Krooneman et al. showed 3-chlorobenzoate is converted to 3-hydroxybenzoate and degraded via gentisate without (chloro)catechol intermediates, but the dehalogenating protein was never purified or cloned, so nothing can be said about mono- versus multifunctionality.
direction_note: Hydrolytic dehalogenation releasing chloride is irreversible; chlorinating 3-hydroxybenzoate with HCl is not a biological reaction, so ModelSEED's '<' is untenable.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - ornithine decarboxylase (ODC1) plus the iodothyronine deiodinases DIO1/DIO2/DIO3
organism_context: mouse and human intestinal tissue; T4 to 3-iodothyronamine (3-T1AM)
rationale: Hoefig et al. demonstrated that 3-T1AM arises from T4 by ODC-catalysed decarboxylation followed by successive deiodinations by DIO1/2/3, so this entry is a whole multi-enzyme route rather than one enzyme; ODC itself is a monofunctional PLP decarboxylase and the deiodinases are separate selenoproteins.
direction_note: Flux is degradative, T4 -> 3-T1AM; the entry additionally drops CO2 and three iodides (ModelSEED flags MI:C:-1/H:4/I:-3/O:-2), so no single enzyme and no thermodynamic estimate can set its direction.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - ornithine decarboxylase (ODC1) plus the iodothyronine deiodinases DIO1/DIO2/DIO3
organism_context: mammalian thyroid hormone metabolism; T3 to thyronamine (T0AM)
rationale: Same lumped route as rxn20971: ODC decarboxylates the iodothyronine and the three deiodinases strip the remaining iodines to give T0AM, so no one protein catalyses this entry; the enzymes that do exist (ODC, DIO1-3) are each monofunctional.
direction_note: The degradative flow is T3 -> T0AM, but with CO2 and three iodides missing (ModelSEED MI:C:-1/H:4/I:-3/O:-2) the ModelSEED '<' call has no enzymological or thermodynamic basis.

enzyme_name: thyroid hormone (aryl/phenol) sulfotransferase - SULT1A1, SULT1E1, SULT1C isoforms
organism_context: human and other mammalian cytosolic sulfotransferases; T4 sulfonation in phase-II hormone inactivation
rationale: Cytosolic SULTs are single-domain ~34 kDa homodimeric proteins with one PAPS site and one sulfuryl-transfer activity; several isoforms sulfonate T4 but each is monofunctional (homodimerisation is not a second activity).
direction_note: PAPS-to-PAP sulfuryl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way; ModelSEED's '<' would run PAP-dependent desulfonation, which SULTs do not do.

enzyme_name: thyroid hormone (aryl/phenol) sulfotransferase - SULT1A1, SULT1E1, SULT1C isoforms
organism_context: human and other mammalian cytosolic sulfotransferases; T3 sulfonation
rationale: Same family of single-domain cytosolic SULTs as rxn20973, here sulfonating T3; one PAPS-binding active site and one catalytic activity per chain.
direction_note: Phase-II sulfonation runs forward with PAPS as donor; the reverse requires a sulfatase, a different enzyme entirely, so the ModelSEED '<' misassigns the chemistry.

enzyme_name: aloenin O-methyl-/O-glucosyl-transferases (uncharacterised); the hexaketide pyrone backbone is made by Aloe arborescens type III PKSs (aloesone synthase / octaketide synthase)
organism_context: Aloe arborescens and other Aloe species, polyketide secondary metabolism
rationale: The pyrone precursor is made by characterised Aloe type III polyketide synthases, but no transferase converting it to aloenin has been isolated, and the conversion needs both O-methylation and O-glucosylation, so there is no single catalysing enzyme to classify.
direction_note: Biosynthesis runs toward aloenin, but the entry uses free D-glucose as the glycosyl donor instead of UDP-glucose and is mass-unbalanced (ModelSEED MI:C:1/H:1/O:-1), so neither direction call rests on real chemistry.

enzyme_name: beta-glucosidase (glycoside hydrolase family 1)
organism_context: plant GH1 beta-glucosidases (AraCyc/Arabidopsis BGLU family) and microbial homologues; 4-methylumbelliferyl-beta-D-glucoside is a synthetic assay substrate
rationale: GH1 beta-glucosidases are single (beta/alpha)8-barrel catalytic domains with one retaining-glycosidase activity. 4-MU-glucoside is a chromogenic reporter rather than a physiological metabolite, so the enzyme is whichever GH1 beta-glucosidase is being assayed and the identification is generic.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is irreversible at cellular water activity; a beta-glucosidase will not condense free glucose with hymecromone, so '<' is not a real enzymatic direction.

enzyme_name: serotonin (phenol) sulfotransferase - SULT1A3, with SULT1A1 contributing
organism_context: human platelet/gut cytosolic sulfotransferases; SULT1A3 is the principal serotonin-sulfonating isoform
rationale: SULT1A3 is a single-domain cytosolic sulfotransferase with one PAPS site that performs only sulfuryl transfer to catecholamine/indolamine phenols; reduced platelet phenol-sulfotransferase activity tracks hyperserotonemia, consistent with a single dedicated activity.
direction_note: PAPS-driven sulfonation of serotonin is one-way; the reverse needs an arylsulfatase, a different protein, so the ModelSEED '<' mislabels the enzymology.

enzyme_name: beta-glucosidase (glycoside hydrolase family 1); esculinase activity
organism_context: plant GH1 beta-glucosidases (AraCyc/Arabidopsis BGLU family) and bacterial esculin-hydrolysing beta-glucosidases
rationale: Esculin is hydrolysed to esculetin and glucose by ordinary GH1 beta-glucosidases, single catalytic-domain retaining glycosidases with one activity; the specific isoform behind this MetaCyc entry is not pinned down, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of the coumarin glucoside is irreversible in vivo; no beta-glucosidase runs the condensation ModelSEED's '<' implies.

enzyme_name: 2'-O-methyllicodione reductase of the retrochalcone (echinatin) pathway - protein not identified
organism_context: Glycyrrhiza echinata (licorice) cell cultures, retrochalcone biosynthesis
rationale: Echinatin biosynthesis in G. echinata is known to run through licodione synthase (a CYP93B P450) and induced O-methyltransferases, but the enzyme reducing 2'-O-methyllicodione to 4,4'-dihydroxy-2-methoxychalcone has never been purified or cloned, so its functionality is unknown.
direction_note: The step is a two-electron reduction yet the equation carries no NAD(P)H (ModelSEED flags MI:H:1/O:-1), so the reductant that would actually fix the direction is absent from the entry.

enzyme_name: 'homovanillate synthase' - no protein of this name identified in the literature
organism_context: L-DOPA / 3-O-methyl-DOPA catabolism (MetaCyc PWY-6334)
rationale: Searches return no enzyme called homovanillate synthase; the step is oxidative decarboxylation of 3-methoxy-4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate to homovanillate, a transformation that also proceeds non-enzymatically with peroxide, so the catalyst (if any) is unidentified.
direction_note: Both the oxidant and the CO2 released are missing (ModelSEED flags MI:C:-1/O:-1); loss of CO2 makes the real transformation one-way toward homovanillate, contrary to ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: staurosporine 4'-N-methyltransferase (StaMA)
organism_context: Streptomyces sp. TP-A0274 / S. longisporoflavus staurosporine gene cluster; related clusters in marine Streptomyces sanyensis
rationale: The staurosporine cluster encodes two separate SAM-dependent methyltransferases, staMA for N-methylation of the 4'-amine of the sugar and staMB for 3'-O-methylation; each is a single-domain methyltransferase and this entry is the StaMA N-methylation (assignment by position in the characterised late-step pathway).
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible forward; '<' would demand SAH-dependent demethylation, which methyltransferases do not perform.

enzyme_name: vibriobactin synthetase (VibB + VibE + VibF + VibH)
distinct_activities: VibF Cy1 - heterocyclisation/dehydration to the methyloxazoline
VibF C2 - condensation at both the primary (N9) and secondary (N5) amines of norspermidine
organism_context: Vibrio cholerae siderophore biosynthesis; reconstituted in vitro from the four purified proteins
rationale: The entry lumps a four-subunit, ten-domain NRPS assembly line, so no single enzyme runs it; polyfunctional applies to the central subunit VibF, one 270 kDa polypeptide with the six-domain organisation Cy1-Cy2-A-C1-PCP-C2 (VibB is separately bifunctional, isochorismatase + ArCP). The four proteins are separate polypeptides, so the system as a whole is a multi-protein pathway rather than a fused enzyme.
direction_note: ATP, which drives the assembly line irreversibly forward, is absent from the equation and no single enzyme catalyses the lumped step, so ModelSEED's '<' has no enzymological basis.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - selenocysteine methyltransferase (SMT) plus downstream C-Se lyase / volatilisation chemistry
organism_context: Se-hyperaccumulating plants (Astragalus, Stanleya) and Se-volatilising soil bacteria and fungi
rationale: Release of dimethyl diselenide from selenocysteine requires methylation followed by lyase/reductive steps carried out by different proteins, so this entry has no catalysing enzyme to classify.
direction_note: The entry is also grossly unbalanced (ModelSEED MI:C:-1/N:-1/O:-2/Se:1 - one Se for a diselenide and no fate for the amino-acid backbone), so no thermodynamic direction call is meaningful in either sense.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme - methionine/Se-methylmethionine methyltransferase (MMT) plus a C-Se lyase releasing dimethyl selenide
organism_context: plant and microbial selenium volatilisation from selenomethionine
rationale: Conversion of selenomethionine to volatile dimethyl selenide proceeds by S-methylation to Se-methyl-selenomethionine followed by a separate cleavage step, so the entry collapses at least two enzymes and no single protein can be named.
direction_note: Volatilisation runs selenomethionine -> dimethyl selenide, but with the whole amino-acid backbone unaccounted for (ModelSEED MI:C:-3/H:-5/N:-1/O:-2) neither direction is thermodynamically interpretable.

enzyme_name: benzoyl-CoA-dihydrodiol lyase / 2,3-epoxybenzoyl-CoA dihydrolase (BoxC)
organism_context: aerobic benzoyl-CoA (box) pathway of Azoarcus evansii and Burkholderia xenovorans LB400
rationale: BoxC is a homodimer of 61 kDa chains, roughly twice a normal crotonase subunit, but the 1.5 A structure shows a single active site in the N-terminal crotonase domain with the duplicated C-terminal region acting only as a structural scaffold; the hydrolytic ring opening and the deformylation are two steps of one overall conversion in that one site, so the MetaCyc 'lyase/hydrolase' name does not mean two independent catalytic activities.
direction_note: Ring cleavage with formate release is catabolic and irreversible; note also that the true substrate is 2,3-epoxybenzoyl-CoA rather than the dihydrodiol written here (Rather et al. 2010).

enzyme_name: 6-hydroxymelatonin sulfotransferase - SULT1A1 (with SULT1A3 and SULT1B1 contributing)
organism_context: human cytosolic sulfotransferases; hepatic melatonin degradation after CYP1A hydroxylation
rationale: Screening of the human cytosolic SULT panel identified SULT1A1 as the main enzyme sulfonating 6-hydroxymelatonin; these are single-domain monofunctional sulfotransferases with one PAPS-binding active site.
direction_note: Phase-II sulfonation with PAPS is effectively irreversible forward; desulfonation requires a distinct sulfatase, so the ModelSEED '<' recommendation does not describe this enzyme.
